bull_bear.body: Focused on capacity expansion (Greenfield/Brownfield) and inorganic growth (integration of Scigenics/C2C). No dividend/buyback commentary; reinvestment mode for scale.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Raw material (metal) price volatility impacting short-term margins. Execution risk on large turnkey projects. High inventory levels (INR 438cr, though <180 days aging) tying up working capital. Geopolitical delays in export shipments.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Highly confident, emphasizing 'best year in history', structural transformation complete, and long-term ambition. Aggressive on capacity and global expansion (Japan+India model).
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Shift to 'pre-cast' civil construction to avoid traditional EPC delays and maintain high-speed project delivery (6 months for blocks). Explicit entry into Nuclear sector confirmed. Japanese ED appointment signals deepening of tech-transfer and global sales channel beyond just sourcing.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- 'Net Debt Free' - total debt/equity fell 1.01, 0.53, 0.32, 0.10, 0.09, 0.10 across FY22-Q1FY27 while net debt/equity went 0.98, 0.47, 0.0, 0.0, 0, 0.
- GScale is '100% Self-Funded - Zero new debt. Leveraging SETL's strong balance sheet (Rs. 105 Cr cash, CRISIL A/Positive).'
- GL Hakko Phase I: 'Rs. 71.5 Cr Capital Deployed', 'Zero External Debt', 'Internal Accruals' as funding source, with majority ownership 'to be achieved over the next 3 years at the same valuation'.
- Returns profile has compressed as equity was raised: ROE 54.9%, 47.6%, 20.7%, 11.6%, 10.7%, 13.2% and adjusted ROE 56.2%, 50.0%, 28.5%, 18.2%, 16.1%, 18.7% across FY22-Q1FY27; ROCE 42.0%, 43.4%, 25.5%, 19.0%, 17.1%, 19.4% with adjusted ROCE 42.5%, 44.1%, 29.4%, 23.8%, 21.1%, 22.7% (adjusted metrics are on average net worth and capital employed net of cash).
- 'Approved raising funds through the preferential issue of up to 24,39,750 equity shares.' The deck states no dividend policy.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Glass-Lined: Core profit driver, ~30% of revenue mix but transitioning. New Products: Shell & Tube Glass-Lined Heat Exchangers (200 units in OB, 100 delivered, local mfg starts July 2026 @ 200 units/month capacity). Bioprocess: Scigenics contributing ~INR 20cr in FY26, targeting INR 60cr in FY27. Engineering: C2C contributed INR 24cr in FY26, targeting INR 60cr in FY27.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Capacity constraint and need for specialized glass-lined/nuclear-grade equipment | Specialty Chemical & CDMO Players | beneficiary | High | SETL's expanded capacity and turnkey capability directly address the capex boom in Indian pharma/chemicals, offering import substitution for complex heat exchangers. |
| Rising input costs and margin pressure | Pure-play Equipment Fabricators | loser | Med | Competitors lacking integrated engineering/subsidiary synergies may struggle to match SETL's solution-based pricing power and margin resilience in FY27. |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- 'A proven, profitable core engine - and a new, high-growth datacenter infrastructure engine bolted onto it' - Engine 1 is turnkey pharma, chemical and agrochemical process equipment; Engine 2 is GScale Energy in AI datacenter power and cooling.
- Engine 1 is described as an 'End to end turnkey engineering solution provider from concept to commission for pharma, chemical and other process industries', a 'Top End to End Solution Provider' serving 'Top 30' listed companies with marquee clients named as Aurobindo, Cipla, Sun Pharma and Dr. Reddy's.
- Moat framing rests on 'AGI's proprietary glass-lining technology' and, via GL Hakko, 'Proprietary glass-lining technology with no direct global equivalent' plus advanced R&D and global technology leadership.
- Operational credentials cited: 99% customer retention rate, 'long-standing relationships in excess of 3 years with 13 of our top 20 customers', and globally certified plants and products (CE Marking, U-Stamp, R-Stamp, PED, NB certified, ISO certified).
- GScale is positioned as a 'Skip-Start' route into AI datacenters - buying 'Years of organic R&D & relationship building' to gain 'Instant Access' to hyperscaler relationships and LOIs and to solve the import gap with Made-in-India giga-watt scale manufacturing.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Rename] Now Standard Engineering Technology Limited, 'Formerly known as Standard Glass Lining Technology Limited', with the 2026 milestone slide recording 'New Name and Change in Object'.
- [Acquisition - GScale] The deck gives two readings of the same transaction: slide 5 and the deal dashboard state a '51% strategic stake' / '51% Equity Stake - Controlling acquisition of GScale Energy', while the business-highlights slide says 'The Company has proposed to acquire controlling stake of 51% in M/s. GScale Energy Private Limited subject to regulatory approvals.(33.55% successfully acquired)'.
- [Acquisition - GL Hakko] 'Completed Phase I of its strategic investment in GL HAKKO Co., Ltd., Japan, acquiring a 19.19% stake. Phase II will increase the stake to up to 51.07% over the next three years, subject to regulatory approvals.' A 'Revenue target of Rs. 400 Cr' is attached to the Scale step of that roadmap, though the deck does not say whose revenue it refers to.
- [Leadership] GScale is led by founder and MD Kasu Brahma Reddy, cited as 25+ years in critical infrastructure, 486 MW delivered and 1 GW+ under execution across Tier-IV facilities, and 'Up to 765/400 kV industry-first power & grid connectivity frameworks'; he is now shown on SETL's leadership team.
- [Governance and ESOP] NRC approved a grant of 6,00,000 ESOPs under the ESOP 2024 Scheme (Grant I); Mr. Yasuyuki Ikeda proposed for redesignation from Non-Executive to Executive Director and Mr. Kancherla Uma Maheswara Rao proposed as Independent Director, both subject to shareholder approval; a subsidiary 'Standard Projects Private Limited' was incorporated.
- [API Pharma UAE] Slide 5 lists 'API Pharma UAE Wholly owned subsidiary' while the 2026 milestone entry describes a '3-year performance agreement with API Pharma (UAE) covering pharma, biopharma, life sciences, F&B & process industries' - the deck does not reconcile the two.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: Q4 Gross Margin declined to 32% (from 39% in Q3) due to metal price volatility and upfront hiring. Management guides margin recovery in FY27 via operating leverage, higher value-add 'solution' selling vs pure equipment, and procurement discipline.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: FY27 expected to be 'better' than FY26 (>26.7%), with quarterly run-rate targeting INR 250-300cr. Margins: Expected to improve in FY27 (>17.4%) driven by operating leverage and solution-mix. Order Inflow: Healthy pipeline, export revenue doubled in FY26, expected to grow further. Capex: INR 130cr over 2 years (INR 65cr in FY27) for Greenfield; INR 35-40cr for brownfield modernization.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Total >INR 1,000cr; Execution timeline 8-10 months. Exports constitute ~INR 30cr currently. Subsidiary C2C holds INR 46-47cr. Mix skewed domestic (>95%).
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Greenfield 36-acre campus (Phase 1 Apr 2027, Phase 2 Apr 2028) adds INR 2,000cr capacity; Brownfield modernization adds another INR 2,000cr; Total target capacity INR 4,000cr. Entry into Nuclear, Oil & Gas, Food & Beverage sectors. Pre-cast building capability to accelerate turnkey project timelines to 6-12 months.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: SETL completed its transformation into an integrated turnkey solutions provider with FY26 revenue up 26.7% to INR 793cr, though Q4 margins dipped to 15.5% due to commodity inflation and preemptive hiring. The INR 1,000cr order book and upcoming INR 130cr capex (targeting INR 4,000cr total capacity) position the company for accelerated FY27 growth, leveraging new Japanese tech partnerships and subsidiary synergies.

open.item: To invest INR25-30 crores in capacity for the Shell & Tube Glass Heat Exchanger product (AGI Japan license).
Quarterly revenue run-rate of INR250-300 crores expected from FY27 onwards.
Promoter share pledge (personal purpose) to be removed within ~6 months, possibly earlier.
Shell-and-tube glass-lined heat exchanger unit to come fully into operation July 1, 2026 (200 units/month capacity); ~50 units already made in India Apr-onward, another 50 in hand.
FY26 export revenue doubled vs FY25; expecting continued export growth in FY27 despite war-related discussion delays.
C2C Engineering FY26 revenue INR24cr, targeting INR60cr FY27 (order book ~INR46-47cr); Scigenics ~INR20cr FY26 targeting INR60cr FY27 — ~INR100cr incremental sales.
To invest another INR35-40cr modernising existing plants (robotic/automatic welding & polishing), adding ~30% capacity (util. now ~70-80%).
EBITDA margin (FY26 17.4%, Q4 15.5%) to improve in FY27 via operating leverage and solution-selling; targeted toward ~16-17%+.
FY27 revenue growth to be better than FY26 (which grew 26.7%); can sustain ~25%+ growth.
New 36-acre campus to open entry into oil & gas, nuclear engineering, food & beverage and heavy precision engineering; nuclear/oil&gas entry expected by FY28.
Export contribution targeted at 15%-20% over the next 2 years (25% possible but not assured).
36-acre greenfield project (two phases): INR130cr total (INR65cr this year, INR65cr next); phase-1 50% operational April 1, 2027, phase-2 April 1, 2028; ~INR2,000cr capacity.
Long-term (10-year) objective to reach 40% exports / 60% domestic revenue mix; targeting 30-40% exports in 5-6 years.
Margin pressure flagged from rising commodity/metal input prices and deliberate manpower investment; to be offset via operating leverage and procurement discipline.
New pre-cast buildings subsidiary (Standard Projects) to speed turnkey project delivery (blocks within ~6 months; projects in 12-14 months) for pharma/chemical clients only — not general EPC/civil.
Existing (modernised) facilities to reach ~INR2,000cr capacity and greenfield another ~INR2,000cr, for a combined ~INR4,000 crores revenue capability.
Inorganic growth to continue alongside organic; more acquisitions planned as part of sustainable growth strategy (per new ED Ikeda).
US tariffs (up to ~25-30%) flagged but assessed as ~18-20% cost impact and not materially damaging since products remain cheaper than US manufacturing.
Shell & tube glass heat exchangers expected to add 30%-40% growth to the glass-lining division revenue.
IPO proceeds of INR210 crores: INR130cr working-capital loan repayment (done), INR40cr capex, INR20cr acquisition, balance general corporate.
